newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israel's Lebanese allies free eight prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Lebanese allies free eight prisoners.

text.p: The Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militia freed eight prisoners on Sunday from its Khiam jail inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, militia sources said.

The SLA sources said the captives were freed as a gesture after New Year and ahead of the Moslem feast of Eid al-Fitr, which marks the end of the fasting month of Ramadan. This year's feast falls early next month.
The prisoners were the first freed this year from the jail and brought the number of releases in two years to 170. About 150 Lebanese and other Arabs are still held without trial at Khiam.
Those freed on Sunday included seven inhabitants of the 15-km (nine-miles) wide border zone, including a woman. The eighth freed captive comes from outside the zone.
Those held in the prison are mostly anti-Israeli guerrillas, villagers who refuse to pay taxes to the SLA, and people who refuse to let their sons be conscripted into the SLA.
Israel carved out the south Lebanon occupation zone in 1985 when it withdrew the bulk of its 1982 invasion force. It is the last active Israeli-Arab front.
